content: A clinical site is a medical facility that is staffed with a clinical investigator, typically a medical doctor (MD), who is qualified to conduct clinical research. To be recognized as a clinical site, the facility must adhere to strict regulations. These regulations are established by the International Conference on Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) and relevant regulatory authorities. These entities provide the guidelines for Good Clinical Practice (GCP) that must be followed at clinical sites. 1. The clinical investigator must possess the necessary qualifications, which include appropriate education, training, and experience, to take responsibility for the proper conduct of the clinical trial. The investigator must meet all qualifications required by applicable regulatory standards and provide evidence of these qualifications through an up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV) or other relevant documentation as requested by the sponsor, the institutional review board (IRB) or independent ethics committee (IEC), and/or the regulatory authority. 2. The investigator must have a thorough understanding of the appropriate use of the investigational product(s). This knowledge should be based on the clinical protocol, the current Investigator’s Brochure, product information, and other resources provided by the sponsor. 3. The investigator must be fully aware of and comply with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and all applicable regulatory requirements. 4. The investigator and/or the institution must allow monitoring and auditing by the sponsor, as well as inspections by the relevant regulatory authorities. 5. The investigator must maintain a list of appropriately qualified individuals to whom significant trial-related responsibilities have been delegated.
